The back corner of the herb loft holds the drying rack at an angle, its four stacked screens each holding a different herb laid flat, the lowest screen's contents already fully dried and beginning to shed onto the frame below it.

A half-tied bundle of dried herb rests on the table with twine fed through from the spool beside it, the loose end held down by a short length of stem, more stems gathered in a rough pile to the left waiting their turn.

A row of brown paper bags stands along one wall of the herb loft, some folded shut and some still open at the top, dried leaf visible inside the nearest one, a small wooden scoop resting against it and crumbled herb scattered on the boards around the group.

A wide copper vat squats at the center of the dairy, its sides streaked with dried whey, a long curd knife laid across its rim and a wooden paddle worn pale resting against the near leg, the scrubbed stone floor beneath it still damp from the morning's work.

The cheese press stands heavy against the far wall, three rounds of fresh curd stacked beneath its weighted board, pale whey still weeping from their edges and pooling in the shallow channel cut into the floor beneath it.

A shelf of ageing wheels lines the cold wall from end to end, their rinds running from pale chalk-white at one end to a deep ochre-grey at the other, the wood beneath them stained dark with years of slow dripping.

A wooden churn sits beside a low stool near the dairy door, its lid fitted loosely across the top, a folded cloth draped over the handle and a shallow bowl of buttermilk resting on the boards beside its curved stave foot.

Cheesecloth hangs in heavy folds from a rod across the corner of the dairy, the lowest corners still dripping into a wide crock set on the floor beneath, the cloth pressed thin where the curds have gathered and the whey is nearly done running.

A stone cooling trough fills the low end of the dairy, four tall cans standing in its cold water up to their necks, a wooden lid resting loose across the nearest one and a long-handled ladle hooked over the trough's edge.

The scrubbed work table holds a wide shallow pan at its center, a thin skim of morning cream still clinging to its inner rim, a slotted spoon and a folded square of cheesecloth lying beside it on the damp boards.

A brine barrel stands in the corner of the dairy, its upper rim crusted pale with dried salt, two small rounds of cheese submerged in the cloudy liquid within it and a flat stone laid across them to hold them under.

Chalk marks climb one of the low beams above the ageing shelf in grouped tallies, pale and crowded, a fresh stick of chalk resting on the shelf's edge below them beside a small wheel still wrapped in its first cloth binding.

A round of pressed curd sits unwrapped on the center of the work table, its surface just beginning to dry at the edges, a curd knife with a long thin blade and a damp cheesecloth folded to a square lying to either side of it.

The ageing shelf nearest the door holds wheels at every stage, the freshest still white and soft-looking at one end and the oldest wearing a grey-green rind at the other, a stiff-bristled brush resting across two of the middle rounds.

A deep wooden mold sits at the edge of the pressing table, its inner walls stained gold from long use, a round of cloth-wrapped curd fitted inside it and the follower board seated on top, waiting for the weight to be set.

Whey runs slowly along a shallow channel in the stone floor, parting around the leg of the work table and disappearing beneath the door of the dairy, the channel's edges pale and encrusted from weeks of the same slow draining.

A low shelf beside the cooling trough holds a row of small crocks stopped with cloth, their sides daubed with dried brine, a stained wooden ladle balanced across two of them and a loose fold of cheesecloth bunched against the wall behind.

The wide vat on the center table sits empty and rinsed, a fine whey smell still rising from its copper sides, the curd knife and the long paddle laid side by side along the table's edge on a damp cloth to dry.

Two wheels of cheese rest on tilted boards against the dairy wall, propped so the rinds can dry evenly on all sides, the older of the two showing a thin grey bloom at its edge and the younger still pale and faintly damp.

A wooden paddle worn pale at its blade and dark at the grip hangs on a peg above the main table, a curd knife with a cracked handle propped beside it, the table below them scattered with dried flecks of whey and a folded cloth.

A cloth-lined mold sits draining over the channel at the corner of the table, its cheesecloth pressed into deep folds by the curd within, a second cloth already folded and waiting beside it and a heavy pressing stone resting on the floor nearby.

The corner of the dairy holds a low rack of drying rounds, the wood of the rack dark and salt-stained, the rinds of the cheese rubbed with a thin coat of brine so they catch the air evenly and the shelf below each round still tacky.

A shallow earthenware pan rests on the end of the work table, a thin curd set firm across its whole surface, a long knife just beginning a cut through its middle and a perforated ladle resting in the pan's handle notch to the side.

A small round of cheese sits wrapped in a clean cloth at the edge of the press table, tied at the top with a loose knot, a damp ring on the wood beneath it where it has been sitting and a spare piece of cloth folded beside it.

The stone floor of the dairy is wet near the press, whey pooled in the low seam between two flags and running slowly toward the wall channel, the press above it still weeping a thin thread from the round stacked beneath its board.

Brine crusts the rim of the soaking barrel in a thick white collar, the liquid inside it deep and cloudy, a small weighted board sitting just below the surface and a handled ladle resting across the barrel's open top.

A curd knife with a long flexible blade lies across the center of the vat, its edge stained faintly yellow, a wooden rib and a folded cheesecloth beside it on the table and a bucket of whey sitting on the floor directly below the vat's spigot.

The ageing shelf at the back of the dairy holds a single very old wheel at its far end, its rind thick and dark and uneven, a stiff brush left resting on it and the shelf wood beneath it stained in rings from months of the same wheel sitting in the same place.
